paper.title: Algorithms with Logarithmic or Sublinear Regret for Constrained Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Unit-cost constrained contextual bandit with known statistics (ALP)
unmapped: finite set of J contexts with i.i.d. arrivals
hard budget B with unit costs; B/T = rho fixed, B and T grow proportionally
dummy skip action
learner knows context distribution pi and expected rewards u_{j,k} (full statistics); regret vs oracle DP policy
best contexts strictly ordered u_1^* > ... > u_J^*
settings.definition_quote: we focus on unit-cost systems, i.e., $c_{j,k} = 1$ for each $j$ and $k$ ... In this section, we study approximations of the oracle, where the statistics of bandits are known to the agent.

settings.name_in_paper: Unit-cost constrained contextual bandit with known context distribution, unknown rewards (UCB-ALP)
unmapped: finite set of J contexts with i.i.d. arrivals, distribution pi known to learner
hard budget B with unit costs, rho = B/T fixed
dummy skip action
regret vs oracle policy with known statistics
best contexts strictly ordered u_1^* > ... > u_J^*
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, a context $X_t$ arrives independently with identical distribution ... the reward $Y_{k,t}$'s are independent random variables in $[0,1]$ ... We assume the agent knows the context distribution

unmapped: two contexts, i.i.d. arrivals, context distribution unknown
hard budget B with unit costs
regret vs oracle policy
settings.definition_quote: When the context distribution and expected rewards are unknown, we propose the UCB-based Procrastinate-for-the-Better (UCB-PB) algorithm for solving the constrained contextual bandit problem with two contexts and unit costs.

settings.name_in_paper: Unit-cost constrained contextual bandit with unknown context distribution, known rewards (EALP2)
unmapped: finite J contexts, i.i.d., distribution unknown
expected rewards u_j^* known to learner
learner knows gap delta between rho and nearest boundary q_j
hard unit-cost budget B
settings.definition_quote: In this section, we relax the assumption of known context distribution and study unit-cost systems with unknown context distribution.

settings.name_in_paper: Constrained contextual bandit with heterogeneous costs (epsilon-First ALP)
unmapped: known fixed heterogeneous costs c_{j,k}
context distribution known
learner knows Delta^* (min gap of ratios xi times min cost difference) and pi_min to set exploration length
finite J contexts with i.i.d. arrivals
settings.definition_quote: we consider the case where the cost for each action $k$ under context $j$ is fixed at $c_{j,k}$, which may be different for different $j$ and $k$.

bound.regime: non-boundary: rho != q_j for all j in {1..J-1}

symbols.u_1_star: highest best-action expected reward among contexts
symbols.u_J_star: lowest best-action expected reward among contexts
symbols.delta_b: min{rho - q_{j~(rho)}, q_{j~(rho)+1} - rho}, distance of rho=B/T to nearest cumulative-probability boundary

source.label: thm:alp_regret
source.quote: Given any fixed $\rho \in (0,1)$, the regret of ALP satisfies: 1) (Non-boundary cases) if $\rho \neq q_j$ for any $j \in \{ 1,2,\ldots, J-1\}$, then $R_{\rm ALP}(T,B) \leq \frac{u_1^* - u_J^*}{1 - e^{-2\delta^2}}$, where $\delta = \min\{\rho - q_{\tilde{j}(\rho)}, q_{\tilde{j}(\rho)+1} -\rho\}$.

results.notes: Regret is vs oracle (optimal policy with known statistics), U* - U_ALP in expectation. Known-statistics planning result.

bound.regime: boundary: rho = q_j for some j in {1..J-1}

source.label: thm:alp_regret
source.quote: 2) (Boundary cases) if $\rho = q_j$ for some $j \in \{1,2,\ldots, J-1\}$, then $R_{\rm ALP}(T,B) \leq \Theta^{\rm (o)} \sqrt{T} + \frac{u_1^* - u_J^*}{1 - e^{-2(\delta')^2}}$, where $\Theta^{\rm (o)} =  2(u_1^* - u_J^*) \sqrt{\rho (1-\rho)}$ ...

bound.regime: non-boundary: rho != q_j for all j in {1..J-1}

source.label: thm:regret_ucb_alp
source.quote: Given $\pi_j$'s, $u_{j,k}$'s and a fixed $\rho \in (0,1)$, the regret of UCB-ALP satisfies: 1) (Non-boundary cases) if $\rho \neq q_j$ for any $j \in \{1, 2, \ldots, J-1\}$, then the regret of UCB-ALP is $R_{\rm{UCB-ALP}}(T, B) = O\big(JK\log T\big)$.

results.notes: J (contexts) mapped to M_ctx. Appendix gives explicit limsup constant Theta^(a) + Theta^(c)_nb with instance-dependent gaps.

bound.regime: boundary: rho = q_j for some j in {1..J-1}

source.label: thm:regret_ucb_alp
source.quote: 2) (Boundary cases) if $\rho = q_j$ for some $j \in \{ 1,2, \ldots, J-1\}$, then the regret of UCB-ALP is $R_{\rm{UCB-ALP}}(T, B) = O\big(\sqrt{T} + JK\log T \big)$.

symbols.Gamma_ctx: sum_{k=1}^K [27/(2 pi_2 Delta^{(1)}_{2,k}) + 2 Delta^{(1)}_{2,k}], with Delta^{(1)}_{2,k} = u_1^* - u_{2,k} and pi_2 the probability of the worse context
symbols.Theta_a: sum_{j=1}^2 sum_{k != k_j^*} [2/Delta^{(j)}_{j,k} + 2 Delta^{(j)}_{j,k}], Delta^{(j)}_{j,k} = u_j^* - u_{j,k}

source.label: thm:regret_ucb_dp
source.quote: For a constrained contextual bandit with unit-cost and two contexts, the UCB-PB algorithm achieves  logarithmic regret as $T$ goes to infinity, i.e., \limsup_{T \to \infty} \frac{R_{\text{UCB-PB}}(T, B)}{\log T} \leq \sum_{k=1}^K \bigg[\frac{27}{2\pi_2\Delta^{(1)}_{2,k}} + 2\Delta^{(1)}_{2,k} \bigg] + \sum_{j=1}^2 \sum_{k \neq k_j^*}\bigg[\frac{2}{\Delta_{j,k}^{(j)}} + 2\Delta_{j,k}^{(j)}\bigg].

results.notes: Holds for both boundary and non-boundary rho. Proof seems to have squared gap in context term; recorded as stated.

bound.regime: non-boundary: rho != q_j; T such that log^3 T / T <= delta^3/(64 J^2)

conditions: log(T)^3/T <= delta^3/(64 J^2) where delta is distance of rho to nearest boundary

source.label: thm:ealp2_regret
source.quote: Given a fixed $\rho \in (0,1)$, $\rho \neq q_j$, $j = 1,2,\ldots, J-1$. If $T_1 = 16 J^2\log^3 T/\delta^2$ and $T$ satisfies $\log^3 T/T \leq \delta^3/(64J^2)$, then the regret of EALP2 satisfies $R_{\rm EALP2}(T,B) = O(1)$.

results.notes: Assumes delta known for presentation; paper sketches a data-driven choice.

tuning: epsilon(T) >= K/((1-delta)pi_min) + log T max{1/delta^2, 16K/((1-delta) pi_min (Delta^*)^2)}, 0<delta<1

source.label: thm:eps_first_alp
source.quote: Let $0 < \delta < 1$. Under $\epsilon$-First ALP, if \epsilon(T) \geq \frac{K}{(1-\delta)\pi_{\min}} + \log T \max\bigg\{\frac{1}{\delta^2}, \frac{16 K}{(1 - \delta)\pi_{\min}(\Delta^*)^2}\bigg\}, then the regret of $\epsilon$-First ALP satisfies: 1) if $\rho = B/T \neq Q_i$, then $R_{\epsilon-\rm First ALP}(T,B) = O(\log T)$;

tuning: epsilon(T) >= K/((1-delta)pi_min) + log T max{1/delta^2, 16K/((1-delta) pi_min (Delta^*)^2)}, 0<delta<1

source.label: thm:eps_first_alp
source.quote: 2) if $\rho = B/T = Q_i$, then $R_{\epsilon-\rm First ALP}(T,B) = O(\sqrt{T})$.
